finding: ALL SIX relevant modules across all three services resolve DB_PATH as a MODULE-LEVEL CONSTANT at import time, not lazily per-call and not via a live-reloaded config object. This is a UNIFORM pattern across the codebase -- no module was found that caches a path or connection in a way that differs from this pattern.

implication_for_real_cutover.symlink_swap_or_env_var_change_alone_is_: If the real P5B switch mechanism turns out to be an atomic symlink swap of database/flex_complete_database.db to point at a new inode (or a change to a DB_PATH env var in supervisord.conf), a process that is ALREADY RUNNING at the moment of the swap would NOT pick up the new target -- it resolved DB_PATH once at its own process start and, in the case of a symlink, likely also holds an already-open sqlite3 connection/file descriptor bound to the OLD inode (POSIX symlink swaps do not retarget already-open FDs).
implication_for_real_cutover.restart_is_mandatory_and_already_planned: This is NOT a new risk discovered here -- it is exactly consistent with why the milestone's own P5B sequence design (Part 12) already places 'quiesce all three -> atomic switch -> start services in proven safe order' AFTER the switch, not before. Every one of the three services necessarily gets a fresh process start (and therefore a fresh DB_PATH resolution + fresh connection) as an inherent, already-required step of the proven quiesce/restart procedure qualified in this R1 (see storage_lifecycle_p5b_r1_three_writer_quiesce_test.json). No additional restart requirement is being newly flagged here beyond what Parts 3-6 already exercise.
implication_for_real_cutover.no_service_requires_special_handling: Because ALL THREE services follow the identical module-level-constant-at-import-time pattern, none of them is a special case requiring extra restart logic beyond the standard supervisorctl stop/start sequence already qualified in Parts 3-6 of this milestone. If a future code change introduced lazy/live DB path resolution (e.g. a config-reload endpoint or a connection pool that re-resolves DB_PATH per-request) for any of these six modules, that WOULD need to be re-audited before relying on this contract -- but no such pattern exists in the current codebase as of this session's inspection.

current_target_verified.no_drift_observed: No module was found pointing at database/_p5a_migration_build/ or any other non-production path; this qualification session did not touch or reference that directory at any point, consistent with the milestone's absolute prohibition on any actual cutover.

verdict: RESTART_TARGET_CONTRACT_PROVEN -- all three services require (and, per this R1's qualified procedure, already receive) a full process restart to pick up any real DB-path change; no service caches a path/connection in a way that would silently survive a symlink swap without restart, so none is flagged as requiring special-case handling beyond the standard proven restart sequence.
